newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESTONIA-BOURSE UPGRADING SYSTEM TO IMPROVE SERVICE.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIA-BOURSE UPGRADING SYSTEM TO IMPROVE SERVICE.

text.p: The Tallinn bourse said on Friday it is working to upgrade its trading system after it went down for thirty minutes when the market opened on Thursday morning.

"The problem this (Thursday) morning was due to one member changing their communication provider on Wednesday night and the stock exchange security system rejecting access," Helo Meigas, managing director of the stock exchange, told Reuters.
"The member did not do enough testing and the server spent the first 10 minutes of the session telling the client that it could not have access, tying up the server up," she added.
The stock exchange, which started operations almost a year ago, is currently upgrading its server software to improve the reliability of the service to members.
"The new server software will also improve the reliabilty and functionality of the system," Meigas said.
Traders were angry over what they described as continuious technical problems when trading was delayed for 30 minutes with some dealers not getting access for almost an hour.
The Tallinn bourse has 18 active trading members.
